children: has started another round of layoffs, affecting roughly 500 employees as the software giant pushes deeper into a sweeping Xbox overhaul while continuing to pour capital into artificial intelligence.

Most of the latest cuts are concentrated in gaming, though a smaller number of jobs in Microsoft's cloud and AI businesses are also affected, according to Business Insider. Within Xbox specifically, Microsoft confirmed it is eliminating 268 positions across Halo Studios, other first-party developers, and management and central functions.
The cuts extend a restructuring announced in July, when Microsoft said it would eliminate roughly 4,800 positions companywide, including 3,200 across Xbox during fiscal 2027.

Xbox chief content officer Matt Booty told employees that the moves completed since July, including studio divestitures, put Microsoft roughly three-quarters of the way through previously announced restructuring.
The shake-up goes considerably deeper than headcount.

Activision will take greater responsibility for major Xbox franchises and is developing the next Halo title through a dedicated team. Bethesda will oversee Obsidian, while Playground Games and Turn 10 are being combined around the Forza and Fable franchises. Microsoft is effectively concentrating more games inside fewer operating groups.
One of the starkest developments involves Ninja Theory, the studio behind the Hellblade franchise.
Microsoft tried twice to sell the studio, but both agreements fell through. The company has now begun consulting employees over a proposed closure while continuing to explore alternatives.

The layoffs arrive as Microsoft balances cost discipline against enormous AI infrastructure spending. Its July cuts came as the company projected roughly $190 billion of 2026 spending, largely as booming Azure and AI demand required more data-center capacity. Microsoft stressed at the time that eliminated jobs were not simply being replaced by AI, though management acknowledged AI is changing how work gets done.

title: Microsoft Sends Stark Message to Xbox Workers
